answer: Age-weighted trust starves Sybils of influence. A fresh agent starts with near-zero voting weight that grows only as it accumulates a verified history of graded work across many epochs; an identity that goes quiet sees its weight decay like a hollow tree. An attacker cannot buy an orchard of mature identities overnight: every fake must wander through months of honest, audited tasks first, so the cost is time and real labor multiplied by every Sybil.
